display.purpose: Aisle numbers, department headers, price numerals, button labels. Signage-register text only.

body.purpose: Item names, descriptions, form copy — everything read at length.

shadows.name: shadow-tag
shadows.purpose: Hard flat offset under the primary button and price tags; disappears with a 2px translate on :active to simulate a tactile press into the signage board.

shadows.name: shadow-card
shadows.purpose: Soft ambient lift, used once for the GeneratingStep card only.

motion.name: reveal-wipe
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) -> inset(0 0 0 0), 0.9s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), respects prefers-reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Left-to-right wipe reveal for the generated redesign image in ResultStep — the one animated entrance in the system.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single forward action a screen owns. Yellow, tactile press on active.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; min-height: 52px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; border: 2px solid #1e211c; background: #f5b400; padding: 12px 28px; font-family: 'Archivo', 'Arial Black', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; color: #1e211c; box-shadow: 0 2px 0 0 #1e211c; transition: all 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(0.95); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(2px); box-shadow: none; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2.5px solid #1e211c; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.4; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Any forward-neutral action that isn't a plain text link.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; min-height: 52px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; border: 2px solid #1e211c; background: #ffffff; padding: 12px 28px; font-family: 'Archivo', 'Arial Black', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; color: #1e211c; transition: background-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #e6e6df; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2.5px solid #1e211c; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Price Tag
components.description: Die-cut yellow tag for hero amounts: budget entry, running totals, final price. Not used for ordinary line-item prices.
components.css: .ds-price-tag { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; font-family: 'Archivo', 'Arial Black', sans-serif; font-weight: 900; line-height: 1; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; background: #f5b400; color: #1e211c; padding: 10px 20px 10px 30px; font-size: 18px; clip-path: polygon(14% 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 14% 100%, 0 50%); } .ds-price-tag::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 9px; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: #f1f1ec; transform: translateY(-50%); }

components.name: Shelf Item Row
components.description: SKU shelf-tag row with a barcode-strip left edge. Used wherever the plan lists a real, priced thing.

components.name: Aisle Header (quiet)
components.description: Collapsed wordmark-only header used for the Design department's three reveal screens, so the generated image reads as the reward, not the signage chrome.
components.css: .ds-aisle-header-quiet { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; border-bottom: 1px solid #d7d7cf; background: #f1f1ec; padding: 16px 64px; } .ds-aisle-quiet-label { font-size: 12px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: #666a5f; }

narrative.overview:
DwellWise reads as a walk down a hardware-superstore aisle — HomePro, ThaiWatsadu signage vocabulary — rather than another glossy before/after AI-photo hero. Every phase of the journey is a numbered department; every priced thing gets a die-cut tag. The system is restrained and daylight-lit: it never goes dark, never goes decorative, and spends its one committed color, safety yellow, only where money or the next action lives.

The one confirmed exception is deliberate: the Design phase (style pick, generated image, before/after result) drops the shelf-tag scaffolding to a quiet wordmark-only header so the generated redesign — the emotional peak of the product — isn't buried under signage chrome. This is a named, built pattern (AisleHeader's quiet variant), not drift.
keyCharacteristics: Daylight retail, never dark: warm off-white ground, no dark-mode surface.
Palette-as-law: yellow (#f5b400) appears only on price and primary action.
Die-cut price tags and barcode-strip shelf rows are the signature units.
2px ink borders, flat corners (no radius) everywhere except round dots/scrollbar.
The aisle-directory header recedes to a quiet bar during the Design department's reveal moments.

rules.name: The Palette-as-Law Rule
rules.body: Yellow spends itself on price and primary action only. If a new element wants yellow for emphasis or decoration, it doesn't get it — use ink, a border, or weight instead.

rules.name: The Budget-State Rule
rules.body: Green and red exist solely to carry the budget-check verdict. They do not double as general-purpose success/error colors elsewhere in the product.

rules.name: The Signage-Face Rule
rules.body: Archivo Black is reserved for things the world would actually print on a sign or a tag — numbers, department names, CTAs. Body copy never uses it.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Borders carry separation everywhere; shadow is reserved for the tactile-press interaction (shadow-tag) and the single ambient-lift moment (shadow-card).

dos: Do reserve yellow (#f5b400) for price and primary action only — the Palette-as-Law Rule.
Do use 2px ink borders and square corners as the default separation and shape language; reach for shadow-tag's hard offset only on tactile, price-bearing controls (buttons, tags).
Do keep the Design department's three reveal screens on the quiet AisleHeader variant so the generated image stays the visual peak.
Do set aisle numbers, department names, and price numerals in Archivo Black, uppercase; keep body copy in IBM Plex Sans.
donts: Don't add rounded corners; the system has none except circular dots/holes and the die-cut clip-path notch.
Don't spend green/red outside the budget-check verdict — they are not general success/error colors.
Don't add a new box-shadow for ordinary card elevation; borders carry depth, and the two existing shadow tokens are each scoped to one specific moment (tactile press, single ambient lift).
Don't apply the display face (Archivo Black) to body prose — it's reserved for signage-register text (numbers, labels, CTAs).
